section_summary: This section documents successive State Department drafts and an article-by-article legal commentary supporting the proposed United States trusteeship of the former Japanese Mandated Islands as a strategic area. The papers address military bases, Security Council supervision, the meaning of “states directly concerned,” inhabitants’ political and civil rights, economic treatment, and the authority to close sensitive areas. They also record American Civil Liberties Union requests for civil government and native-language education, and a Soviet objection that trusteeship should await the Allied peace settlement with Japan.

subfiles.title: Conclusion of an earlier draft statement submitting the trusteeship agreement
subfiles.from: Herschel Johnson, incorporating a message from James F. Byrnes
subfiles.about: The statement defends strategic-area trusteeship and asks the Security Council to refer the proposed agreement to a committee of the whole.
subfiles.summary: The concluding pages argue that disputes over which states are “directly concerned” should not delay approval. They explain the territory’s strategic designation, proposed bases, application of Charter Articles 43, 87, and 88, and protections for political, economic, social, and educational advancement. The speaker concludes by moving that the draft agreement be considered by a committee of the whole.

subfiles.title: Memorandum transmitting a revised draft statement
subfiles.to: Trusteeship working-group members, including Mr. Gross, Mr. Bancroft, Mr. Hiss, Mr. Borton, Mr. Blaisdell, Mr. Howard, Captain Dennison, and Colonel Giffen
subfiles.about: Green circulates a revised statement for a working-group meeting and asks recipients to disregard the preceding draft.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum says the attached revision incorporates additional ideas received from Herschel Johnson and Mr. Gerig in New York. It was prepared for discussion at the working group’s Friday meeting and supersedes the version distributed on the preceding Monday.

subfiles.title: Fourth Draft: Submission to the Security Council of the United States Draft Trusteeship Agreement for the Japanese Mandated Islands
subfiles.about: The fourth draft presents the historical, legal, strategic, and humanitarian case for United States administration of the Japanese Mandated Islands.
subfiles.summary: The draft traces American support for mandates and trusteeship from Wilson through Roosevelt and explains the November 1946 announcement of proposed United States administration. It urges waiver of disputes over “states directly concerned,” designates the whole territory as strategic, and defends bases, most-favored-nation treatment, and controlled access to security areas. It also stresses political, economic, social, and educational advancement and proposes committee consideration of the agreement.

subfiles.title: Memorandum transmitting the draft commentary on the trusteeship agreement
subfiles.about: Green forwards a revised article-by-article commentary and flags issues arising from debate over the New Zealand agreement for Western Samoa.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum states that the commentary was revised after the November 20 meeting and reflects suggestions from the commercial-policy and aviation divisions. Because of controversy in New York over Article 10 of the Western Samoa draft, Green proposes confidential notes under Articles 1 and 5 for discussion at the next meeting.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of commentary to the Deputy United States Representative to the Security Council
subfiles.to: Deputy Representative of the United States to the Security Council, New York
subfiles.about: The Acting Secretary transmits an interpretive memorandum for use during Security Council consideration of the trusteeship agreement.
subfiles.summary: The cover letter explains that the enclosure interprets every article of the proposed agreement. It notes that the treatment of the preamble and Articles 8 and 13 is especially detailed because those provisions are expected to attract questions in the Security Council.

subfiles.title: Commentary on the United States Trusteeship Agreement for the Japanese Mandated Islands
subfiles.to: Deputy Representative of the United States to the Security Council
subfiles.about: The memorandum interprets the preamble and all sixteen articles of the proposed strategic trusteeship agreement.
subfiles.summary: The commentary explains the legal basis for transferring the former mandate to United States trusteeship and argues against naming multiple “states directly concerned” under Article 79. It defends strategic designation, sole United States administration, broad administrative and military powers, bases and forces, inhabitants’ advancement and civil freedoms, and most-favored-nation economic treatment. Further sections address customs and administrative unions, regional cooperation, territorial citizenship, legislation, international conventions, Security Council and Trusteeship Council supervision, closed security areas, amendment, and entry into force. Confidential notes anticipate Soviet, Chinese, and Indian arguments that bases must await an Article 43 agreement and recommend resisting that interpretation.

subfiles.title: Memorandum forwarding Dulles and Duggan correspondence
subfiles.about: Green circulates two letters raising civil-liberties concerns about the proposed trusteeship agreement.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum reports that Mr. Gerig forwarded letters from John Foster Dulles and Laurence Duggan. Green suggests considering them while preparing for action on the Japanese Mandated Islands agreement. The attachments are identified as Dulles’s November 30 letter to Roger Baldwin and Duggan’s November 26 letter to Senator Warren Austin.

subfiles.title: Letter from John Foster Dulles to Roger N. Baldwin
subfiles.to: Roger N. Baldwin, American Civil Liberties Union
subfiles.about: Dulles explains that the trusteeship agreement lies outside the General Assembly delegation’s jurisdiction but promises to relay the ACLU’s concerns.
subfiles.summary: Dulles acknowledges Baldwin’s November 26 letter and its enclosure from Laurence Duggan to Senator Austin. Because the State Department prepared the terms for direct submission to the Security Council, he says the matter is not within his General Assembly delegation’s jurisdiction. He nevertheless undertakes to bring Duggan’s point to State Department officials.

subfiles.title: Letter from Laurence Duggan to Senator Warren Austin
subfiles.from: Laurence Duggan, Committee on Civil Rights in American Colonies
subfiles.to: Senator Warren Austin, Chairman of the United States Delegation to the United Nations General Assembly
subfiles.about: Duggan asks that the trusteeship agreement guarantee civil government and education in native languages.
subfiles.summary: The letter states that the ACLU’s concern is the extension of American civil liberties to the islanders rather than the political form of trusteeship. Duggan argues that the agreement gives no assurance of civil government and warns against continuing unappealable naval rule of the kind experienced in Guam and Samoa. He also condemns compulsory English-language instruction and requests amendments protecting education in native languages.

subfiles.title: Memorandum transmitting a new draft statement
subfiles.about: Green circulates a new statement revised after the working group’s latest discussion.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum says the new draft reflects the discussion at the preceding meeting. It notes that the pages following the presidential statement incorporate the principal arguments from Mr. Cohen’s draft statement.

subfiles.title: Sixth Draft: Submission to the Security Council of the United States Draft Trusteeship Agreement for the Japanese Mandated Islands
subfiles.from: Herschel Johnson, transmitting a message from James F. Byrnes
subfiles.about: The sixth draft offers a revised public defense of immediate United States strategic trusteeship over the former Japanese mandate.
subfiles.summary: The statement reviews the development of international trusteeship and asserts that Japan violated its mandate by converting the islands into bases for aggressive war. It argues that the United States, as present occupant and proposed sole administrator, may submit the agreement without the prior assent of other interested states, while promising to consider their views. The draft emphasizes the territory’s strategic importance, the need for bases, safeguards for inhabitants, and international supervision except where security requires restrictions. It concludes by recommending referral to a committee of the whole.

subfiles.title: Memorandum transmitting the Soviet note and a proposed responsive paragraph
subfiles.about: Green circulates a Soviet objection to immediate trusteeship and a proposed addition to Herschel Johnson’s statement answering it.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum summarizes the Soviet position that trusteeship for both the mandated islands and any other Japanese islands should be considered by the Allied Powers during the peace settlement with Japan. It attaches a translation of the December 7 Soviet Embassy note and a new paragraph intended for discussion at the next working-group meeting.

subfiles.title: Soviet Embassy note on trusteeship for Japanese islands
subfiles.from: F. Orekhov, Chargé d’affaires ad interim of the USSR in the United States
subfiles.to: Dean Acheson, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The Soviet Government states that the trusteeship question should be handled by the Allied Powers as part of the Japanese peace settlement.
subfiles.summary: The note acknowledges the American communication of November 6 and says the Soviet Government needs to study the issue and the American draft agreement. Although prepared to consider United States interests, Moscow maintains that trusteeship over the former mandate and any other Japanese islands must be considered by the Allied Powers in connection with the peace settlement with Japan.

subfiles.title: Suggested addition to the sixth draft of Herschel Johnson’s statement
subfiles.about: The proposed paragraph answers the Soviet contention that trusteeship must await a general peace treaty with Japan.
subfiles.summary: The addition explains that the November announcement was made so United Nations members considering other mandates would know the American position. It argues that Japan’s September 2, 1945 surrender and acceptance of the Potsdam Declaration allow Japanese islands to be placed under trusteeship without waiting for a general peace settlement. It then resumes the argument that the United States should take the initiative in drafting terms for the former mandate.
